title: One quarter of a set
objective: Find one quarter of a set of things.
summary: Adults practice finding one quarter of a set by marking items on a rendered set, with familiar references and adaptive support.

audience.description: Adults who want to feel confident with everyday fractions.

prerequisites.text: Split a set into equal groups and count how many are in each group.

essential_facts.text: One quarter means the whole set split into 4 equal groups, taking 1 of those groups.
Start from the whole set: count everything before you take a part.
To find one quarter of a number of things, divide that number by 4.

contexts.label: Work project
contexts.scenario_template: Your {{whole}} has {{total}} {{item_plural}}. Mark {{fraction_text}} of the {{item_plural}} as {{state}}.
contexts.limits: Tasks differ in size in real projects; here every task counts the same, so a quarter is about how many tasks, not how much work.

contexts.label: Sharing materials
contexts.scenario_template: A {{whole}} holds {{total}} {{item_plural}}. Mark {{fraction_text}} of the {{item_plural}} as {{state}}.
contexts.limits: Sharing usually means equal shares for several people; here we take one share and leave the rest in the box.

contexts.label: Sports season
contexts.scenario_template: A team plays {{total}} {{item_plural}} in a {{whole}}. Mark {{fraction_text}} of the {{item_plural}} as {{state}}.
contexts.limits: Only works if the learner knows how a season of matches works; results depend on play, here we only count matches.

confusions.description: Reads 1/4 as a number of things to take (1 thing, or 4 things) instead of a share of the whole.
Marks the part that is left over instead of the asked part.
Close to the right amount; likely a counting slip rather than a misunderstanding.

essential.title: The key idea
essential.body_template: One quarter of {{total}} {{item_plural}} means splitting all {{total}} into 4 equal groups and taking 1 group. Count carefully: you need {{part_size}} {{item_plural}}.

worked-example.title: Worked example
worked-example.body_template: Here is one worked through. The {{whole}} has {{total}} {{item_plural}}. Split them into {{group_count}} equal groups of {{group_size}}. One group is {{part_size}} {{item_plural}}, so {{fraction_text}} of {{total}} is {{part_size}}.

step-by-step.title: One step at a time
step-by-step.body_template: Let's go in small steps with the {{total}} {{item_plural}}.
steps_template: First, how many {{item_plural}} are there in total? {{total}}.
A quarter means 4 equal groups. How many go in each group? {{total}} ÷ 4 = {{group_size}}.
Now take 1 of those groups: mark {{part_size}} {{item_plural}}.

contrast.title: Which part is asked?
contrast.body_template: Compare the two parts. {{fraction_text}} of {{total}} is {{part_size}} {{item_plural}}. The part that is left is {{remaining}} {{item_plural}}. The task asks for the {{part_size}}, not the {{remaining}}.

prerequisite-check.title: Equal groups first
prerequisite-check.body_template: Before quarters, a quick check on equal groups: {{total}} {{item_plural}} shared into 4 equal groups gives {{group_size}} in each group.

must: Speak to an adult, plainly and respectfully.
Describe what happened in the task, never what the person is.

tests.name: any five of twenty is one quarter
one item reads the fraction as a count
the remaining part is not the asked part
